root_cause.text: In `regulator_resolve_supply()` the late-enable failure path cleared `rdev->supply` and released it with `_regulator_put()` without holding the regulator core’s required locking (`regulator_list_mutex`/`rdev` locks), creating an unsafe race and lockdep violation in the regulator subsystem.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `_regulator_put(rdev->supply)` with `regulator_put(supply)` and adds `regulator_lock_two(rdev, rdev->supply->rdev, &ww_ctx)` / `regulator_unlock_two(...)` around `rdev->supply = NULL`, while the CVE text says `_regulator_put()` “must be held when calling” with `regulator_list_mutex` and warns that “no concurrent access happens to our rdev while we clear out the supply pointer.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the regulator enable failure cleanup by clearing and releasing the supply under proper locking before dropping the reference.
intent_record.what: In the error path after `regulator_enable(rdev->supply)` fails, the code no longer directly calls `_regulator_put(rdev->supply)`. Instead, it acquires a dual-regulator lock with `regulator_lock_two(rdev, rdev->supply->rdev, &ww_ctx)`, saves `rdev->supply` into a local `supply` variable, sets `rdev->supply = NULL`, unlocks both regulators with `regulator_unlock_two(rdev, supply->rdev, &ww_ctx)`, and then calls `regulator_put(supply)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the failure cleanup path so the supply pointer is cleared while holding the appropriate regulator locks, reducing the risk of concurrent access or lock-order issues during error handling. It preserves the intended cleanup behavior but makes it safer by synchronizing the transition before releasing the regulator reference.
